Confirmed. My check was wrong about how to read the branch, not about the paths. GitHub code search indexes the default branch only, which is `dev`, so it returns nothing for v2. The git tree API at `refs/heads/v2` shows both files: `packages/core/src/formatter/builtins.ts` and `packages/core/src/config/plugin/formatter.ts`.

v2 resolves the override with `builtIns.find((formatter) => formatter.name === name)`, so this bug is already fixed there. #46869 only helps the `dev` line.

v2 is also where the work lands. Of the last 40 merged pull requests, 36 target `v2` and 4 target `dev`. The v2 `AGENTS.md` says the default branch is `v2` and that pull requests should target `v2`. The `dev` copy still names `dev`, which is why I read that one.

One defect does carry over to v2. `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/edit.ts` compares `input.oldString === input.newString` on the raw input near the top. It converts both strings to the file's line ending about thirty lines below that check. So a CRLF file takes `oldString` spelled CRLF and `newString` spelled LF past the guard. After the conversion the two are equal. The edit then writes the file back unchanged and reports one replacement. That is what #46849 fixes on `dev`, and the same gap is in the new file.

`packages/opencode` does not exist on v2, so #46860 is a `dev` line fix only.

I'm also very interested in this feature as this would solve an existing problem I'm having. Regarding your question, I'm okay with the second option - returning no skills on the first run and picking them up on the next load. The reason being that I find opencode sessions tend to be rather ephemeral and reloading isn't a huge issue. As the git repo gets updated, the clone will keep updating and skills will keep popping up. Having a delay by one session isn't a huge deal and a lesser deal that blocking for the clone IMHO.

Updated in d220fff39325dd3252fbc05008202e283c9ad789.

- Open-file, file, and preview tabs now have a **4px trailing inset**, matching the 4px top/bottom clearance around their 20px close controls. The existing 4px label-to-close gap is unchanged; context and terminal tabs are untouched.
- Replaced `plus-small` with the same outline glyph used by session tabs (`plus` in the current icon catalog; there is no registered `outline-plus` key).
- Extended the file-browser regression test to cover the icon and all three tab insets.

### Before / after

Real web app, dark theme, 1440×900 viewport, 2× scale, 100% zoom, en-US, reduced motion. Both refs used the same mocked backend/project and persisted session/panel setup. Open, preview, pin, close, reopen, keyboard close, and file-search focus behavior passed. Browser geometry confirmed top/bottom/right clearances changed from **4/4/8px → 4/4/4px** for all three tab states.

- Before: `1512668f6b1a4f63ba0b0130d177bb1ef6f9bedd`
- After: `d220fff39325dd3252fbc05008202e283c9ad789`
- Each crop is 460×72px; the pixel changes are confined to the trailing edge and plus icon (1.76% of each crop).

![Open-file, preview, and file tabs: before, after, and pixel diff showing the tighter trailing inset and standard plus glyph](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/434fe542bd0bb2d90ab4b91c1a4929381d789f77/file-tab-inset-comparison.png)

### Checks

- App/UI typechecks and E2E typecheck passed.
- `review-open-file.spec.ts` and `file-browser-sidebar-tab-switch.spec.ts`: **2 passed**. The new icon assertion failed against the original code before the fix.
- Prettier and `git diff --check` passed.
- Production tab-switch benchmark caveat: the five-scenario suite had a source-timeline markdown-readiness timeout on both refs (4/5 passed in the final full runs). The timed-out after scenario passed in isolation. This is **not a clean full benchmark run or a performance claim**.
Closing for now: this implementation adds more complexity than we want to carry for this edge case. The reproduction and tests remain available here if we revisit it later.

Confirmed against OpenCode Zen on Windows after upgrading the CLI to v1.18.27.

This is an account-scoped provider-catalog gap, not a stale local config:

- The authenticated `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models` response contains 8 models, including `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` and `muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free`.
- The current Zen workspace has Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor Free enabled.
- `opencode models --refresh` succeeds but still omits `opencode/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free`; it only lists Muse 1.2 / 1.2 Contributor Free.
- `opencode models stealth --refresh` reports `Provider not found: stealth`, even though the Zen workspace UI exposes the relevant upstream provider as Stealth.
- The active Zen profile has no explicit `model` or `models` map, so this is not a local allow-list.

The public Zen docs name the same model ID and document the authoritative model endpoint: https://dev.opencode.ai/docs/zen

For Zen specifically, the desired reconciliation behavior is:

1. fetch the authenticated `/zen/v1/models` response during provider discovery;
2. use that account/workspace-scoped response to add and remove selectable `opencode/<id>` models;
3. merge static metadata from models.dev when present, but do not hide endpoint-only models;
4. retain a last-known-good cache with a visible freshness state when the endpoint fails;
5. expose the same resolved list to ACP clients such as Zed after a new agent connection.

This directly covers a model that is enabled for the account and officially documented, but cannot currently appear in the local picker without a manual configuration entry.

Follow-up: the Zen model itself is healthy; the failure is client-side catalog/metadata integration.

Using the same stored Zen credential, a minimal direct request to the documented endpoint succeeded:

```text
POST https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/responses
model: muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free
input: Reply with exactly: MUSE13_OK
```

The response had an ID and contained `MUSE13_OK`.

Therefore the account/workspace authorization and the upstream Muse 1.3 service are working. The `UnknownError` from `opencode run --model opencode/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free ...` is not an upstream availability failure; it is consistent with the client failing to discover the endpoint-only model and consequently selecting/building the wrong request metadata or route.

This strengthens the requested regression: resolve model metadata from authenticated Zen discovery, then verify that a model returned by discovery can execute through the stock OpenCode client path without any manual `provider.models` entry.

Additional verification for the Zen case: the exact endpoint-only ID `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` succeeds through a minimal direct request to the documented Zen Responses endpoint with the same credential. The local stock OpenCode client fails only because its refreshed catalog omits the model. This confirms that endpoint discovery must provide enough route/SDK metadata for the normal client execution path, not merely add a display entry.

I can confirm that it is still important that OpenCode be usable offline (e.g. with on-device inference) even when my configuration includes well-known credentials for online-only providers. I run a community-specific provider that gets non-technical users onboard via the well-known route, but it undermines my story about how OpenCode is going to offer them resilience when it falls apart offline. Just having the associated config go ignored when unavailable is much preferred to failing to launch.

(I can imagine some scenarios where a remote config is somehow being used to lock down the general behavior of OpenCode, and letting it launch when the remote config is missing bypasses that lock-down. But who is actually using remote configs in that way? I'd rather a fail-open than fail-closed design for something like OpenCode that is user-centered rather than provider-centered.)

Agreed on the split, and #37043 is still open.

The `NO_PROXY`/loopback half does overlap with #37043 — same symptom, same missing wiring of the `proxy-env.ts` resolver. As the bot notes, the `NODE_OPTIONS=--dns-result-order=ipv4first` half is not covered there: the compiled Bun binary silently drops that flag, which is a separate defect from proxy resolution and needs either support or an explicit documented limitation.

PR #47093 addresses the loopback-proxy half only and is deliberately scoped to that, so it can land against #37043's description without waiting on a DNS decision. If maintainers want the proxy half tracked solely on #37043, I will retarget #47093 there and keep this issue open for the DNS-order behavior alone — that keeps the two independently actionable rather than blocking one on the other.

Distinct from all three, and none of them has landed — #37617, #45159 and #31137 are all still open.

Those three describe the toggle being **disabled / forced off**: the control itself is unavailable or gets reset by layout switching. This issue is the inverse failure — the toggle reads **ON** and still does not suppress prompts, so the UI state and the runtime permission state disagree in the direction that looks like it should work.

That matters because the disabled-toggle reports are fixable in the settings UI alone, whereas this one is a propagation bug: the persisted setting is never applied to a newly created session. PR #47104 fixes exactly that path (settings auto-accept honored when a session is created), so it does not overlap with a UI-enablement fix.

Happy to close as a duplicate if a maintainer prefers to track the ON-but-ignored case under #37617, but the reproduction and the fix are different from the disabled-toggle ones.

Both cited issues are still open, and neither covers this one.

- #30611 is about *whether* transient network errors get retried at all — retry policy inside OpenCode.
- #42513 asks for built-in auto-failover on rate limits — a feature request for OpenCode-side failover.

This issue is narrower and is a prerequisite for both: the session error object **loses the HTTP status** when a provider failure is wrapped as `UnknownError`. Whatever retries — OpenCode's own logic in #30611, the failover in #42513, or an external plugin — cannot classify 401 vs 429 vs 503 if the status was already discarded at the wrap site. Fixing the wrap does not implement either of those features, and implementing either of them without the status still leaves the classifier blind.

PR #47092 preserves the status on the Error wrap and does not change retry policy, which keeps it independent of the decisions still open on #30611 and #42513.

#45788 is the same root cause and is still open. This issue was filed as the replacement for auto-closed #20895 and carries the fix in PR #47098.

Rather than duplicate the report, I am happy for this to be treated as the implementation ticket for #45788: PR #47098 serves `OPENCODE_WEB_DIST` ahead of the hosted web UI, which is the concrete resolution for the behavior #45788 describes. If maintainers prefer, close this one and I will re-point #47098 at #45788 — the code change is unaffected either way.

Additional root-cause evidence from OpenCode Desktop on Windows:

When the model is surfaced through an empty `provider.opencode.models["muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free"]` entry, Desktop logs that it selected `OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel` and then retries `Internal server error`.

That is the wrong transport for this Zen model. The catalog metadata identifies the model package as `@ai-sdk/openai`, and the Zen documentation specifies the Responses endpoint. A direct minimal request to `/zen/v1/responses` succeeds with the same credential.

So discovery cannot merge endpoint IDs as empty model entries: it must also retain or derive the per-model SDK/transport metadata. Otherwise a missing catalog entry becomes both a picker omission and a runtime misrouting bug.

Update: inspected local checkout (1.18.27). There IS already a non-interrupting queue manager: `session.queued_prompts` (`packages/tui/src/config/keybind.ts:102`, default `<leader>q` / `ctrl+x q`) opening the `queued-menu` (`footer.view.tsx:323`) where queued prompts can be deleted without interrupting the running turn. The statusline also shows `${queue()} queued` (`footer.view.tsx:466`).

So this issue is more about discoverability/binding than missing functionality. Workaround is binding `session_queued_prompts` to `shift+escape` in `tui.json` for parity with Claude Code/Codex `Shift+Esc` (leaving `Esc` as `session_interrupt`). I added that locally:

```json
{ "keybinds": { "session_queued_prompts": "ctrl+x q, shift+escape" } }
```

Suggest either rebinding default or documenting the distinction (`Esc` = interrupt running, `Shift+Esc`/ `<leader>q` = dequeue only) in https://opencode.ai/docs/keybinds and https://opencode.ai/docs/tui.
